subject: simple tags, iterators, and conditional iterators in the init statement

messages.author: a3507002594986dd
messages.subject: simple tags, iterators, and conditional iterators in the init statement
parts:
Hello,

I am setting up the init section to create a series of Mplus input files and was wondering about these 2 questions:

1) After iterators are defined, can I use a simple tag to define other variables computed from iterator values? Essentially, these 'other' variables become iterators too but I'm not sure how to specify them. For example the resvarY variable below:

[[init]]
iterators = J m Rsq corXX Rsq;
J = 10 30 50;
m = 5 10 20;
Rsq = .05 .10 .20;
corXX = .20 .40;
resvarY = 1-Rsq;
etc...
[[/init]]

2) Is there a way to code conditional loops within the [[init]] code to define a variable that essentially also becomes an iterator? Specifically, I have one variable in particular that has been pre-computed and depends jointly on values of two of my iterators. Something like this:

[[init]]
iterators = J m Rsq corXX Rsq;
J = 10 30 50;
m = 5 10 20;
Rsq = .05 .10 .20;
corXX = .20 .40;
resvarY = 1-Rsq;
[[Rsq = .05]]
[[corrXX = .20]]
coeff = valuehere;
[[/corrXX = .20]]
[[/Rsq = .05]]
etc...setting conditionals for all four combinations of corrXX an Rsq...
[[/init]]

I know the above code does NOT work (I tried it) so any help you can give would be very much appreciated!!

Thank you in advance!

Best,
Liz

messages.author: a3507002594986dd
messages.subject: Re: simple tags, iterators, and conditional iterators in the init statement
parts:
Forgive my multiple messages -- but for those interested -- I checked in with four folks I know who use Mplus Automation and all use regular R code loops for setting iterative conditions prior to creating input files. In either words, they did not have a direct answer to my questions. What I ended up doing was taking the two issues out of the [iters] portion of the file generation and using the DEFINE command within the Mplus portion of the code. Within the DEFINE command I used computations on the iterators for mathematical definitions (issue #1), and the two conditionals on the iterators to create the known variable (issue #2). All is working well now!

Best,
Liz
